chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abān, from Al-Sadūsi, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to me as a visitor (for Ziyārah), I will be his intercessor on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Ziyarah to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarah* underscores the unique status of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.a.w.) as an intercessor, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theology where his love and visitation serve as a means of divine proximity. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of early Kufan and Qummi scholars in preserving this promise of *shafa'ah* (intercession) for those who honor his memory. This act of Ziyarah is not merely physical but a spiritual commitment that secures his advocacy on the Day of Judgment.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abān, from Al-Sadūsi, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), who said:
The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) said: On the Day of Judgment, I will intercede for those who have come to my Ziyārah.
